summary: The note describes how Benito Mussolini's rise to power in Italy in 1922 changed colonial government in Eritrea. After Mussolini declared the Italian Empire in May 1936, Italian Eritrea, enlarged with northern Ethiopian regions, was merged with Italian Somaliland and newly conquered Ethiopia into Italian East Africa. The Fascist period is framed as imperial expansion in the name of a 'new Roman Empire'.
one_line: Overview of how Mussolini's Fascist rule and the 1936 declaration of empire reshaped Italian Eritrea within Italian East Africa.
key_facts: Benito Mussolini's rise to power in Italy in 1922 brought profound changes to the colonial government in Eritrea.
Mussolini, referred to as 'il Duce', declared the birth of the Italian Empire in May 1936.
Italian Eritrea was enlarged with northern Ethiopia's regions before the merger.
Italian Eritrea and Italian Somaliland were merged with the just conquered Ethiopia.
The merged territory was named the new Italian East Africa, in Italian 'Africa Orientale Italiana'.
The merger into Italian East Africa followed the declaration of the Italian Empire in May 1936.
The Fascist period was characterized by imperial expansion in the name of a 'new Roman Empire'.
